articles.title: Mystery Solved: Glowing Object Over North India Was Chinese Rocket Debris, Not Meteor
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dazzling light seen over parts of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Delhi-NCR around 1:20 am on September 19 was confirmed as satellite debris, not a meteor.

body.html:
A dazzling light seen over parts of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Delhi-NCR around 1:20 am on September 19 was confirmed as satellite debris, not a meteor.

Astronomers revealed that the spectacle matched the re-entry of China’s Long March 3B rocket (CZ-3B R/B, ID 61188), which had been predicted to fall back to Earth the same day. The fragments burned brightly while entering the atmosphere, creating a glowing trail visible across cities including Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram, Jaipur, and Aligarh.

Nehru Planetarium in Delhi confirmed it was not a shooting star but disintegrating satellite debris. The American Meteor Society and Aerospace Corporation also backed this explanation.

The rare sight left residents stunned, with videos flooding social media before experts settled the debate.

articles.title: Kanpur man strangled live-in girlfriend, dumped body in suitcase in Yamuna — shocking confession
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kanpur: A 20-year-old woman, Akanksha (also called Mahi) of Sujnipur village, Rura, Kanpur Dehat, was strangled to death by her live-in boyfriend, Suraj Kumar, police said.

body.html:
Kanpur: A 20-year-old woman, Akanksha (also called Mahi) of Sujnipur village, Rura, Kanpur Dehat, was strangled to death by her live-in boyfriend, Suraj Kumar, police said. After killing her, Suraj and an accomplice, Ashish Kumar, packed the body into a suitcase and dumped it in the Yamuna near Banda, about 100 km away.

DCP (South) Deependra Nath Chaudhary said Akanksha’s mother, Vijayshree, filed a missing person report at Hanumant Vihar police station on August 8. Police later detained Suraj and, during interrogation, he confessed. He told investigators he had another girlfriend and that Akanksha had discovered his WhatsApp chats. He admitted that, following an argument on July 21, he strangled Akanksha in their room, called Ashish to help, and disposed of the body from Chilla bridge at about 2:30 am.

Suraj allegedly misled the family for three days by sending messages from Akanksha’s phone. He later dropped the victim’s phone on a train, he told police. Officers say Suraj broke down and confessed after being confronted with mobile location data and call records. A kidnapping case was registered on the mother’s complaint; further legal action is underway.

articles.title: Mathura Man Arrested for Threatening to Kill UP CM Yogi Adityanath in Viral Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mathura, Uttar Pradesh: A 27-year-old man, Suneet alias Gatua from Nagla Hardayal village, was arrested after posting a viral video on social media threatening to kill UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.

body.html:
Mathura, Uttar Pradesh: A 27-year-old man, Suneet alias Gatua from Nagla Hardayal village, was arrested after posting a viral video on social media threatening to kill UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. In the video, uploaded on 19 September, Suneet held a country-made pistol to his head, claiming he would shoot the CM by 25 September before turning the gun on himself.

Police traced Suneet to his residence, where he climbed to the terrace with the pistol, fired shots in the air, and threatened self-harm, leading to a tense two-hour standoff. Authorities eventually apprehended him and recovered a .32-bore country-made pistol and live cartridges.

The accused reportedly acted out of frustration over inaction on a prior complaint against his uncle regarding a land dispute. Police indicated that Suneet is a habitual drinker and may have been under the influence, though toxicology reports are pending. Local residents noted signs of mental stress and erratic behavior in recent months.

An FIR has been registered at Mant police station under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for criminal intimidation, illegal possession of arms, and attempt to incite violence. Investigations are ongoing to determine how Suneet obtained the firearm and whether any substances influenced his actions.

The case drew significant attention due to the direct death threat to a sitting Chief Minister and the dramatic standoff that unfolded publicly.

articles.title: Ayodhya Police Bust Sex Racket Near Police Station, Several Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh: In a major crackdown, Ayodhya police busted a sex racket operating from a guest house in Kheer Wali Gali, just a few steps from the Fatehganj police station. The raid took place late Friday night following complaints from concerned residents.

body.html:
Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh: In a major crackdown, Ayodhya police busted a sex racket operating from a guest house in Kheer Wali Gali, just a few steps from the Fatehganj police station. The raid took place late Friday night following complaints from concerned residents.

Police arrested six girls and some boys from the premises. The girls, reportedly trafficked from Bihar and Gorakhpur, were taken to the women’s police station. The guest house operator, Ganesh Agarwal, is under questioning, and further investigation is underway to identify others involved.

City Circle Officer Shailendra Singh stated that strict action will be taken against all those involved in the racket. The operation was led by several outpost in-charges under the supervision of the City Superintendent of Police.

articles.title: Ajmer Shocker: Mother Throws 3-Year-Old Daughter Into Anasagar Lake After Partner’s Taunts
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ajmer police have arrested a 28-year-old woman, accused of killing her 3-year-old daughter by drowning her in Anasagar Lake. The shocking incident came to light after CCTV footage exposed contradictions in her statement.

body.html:
Ajmer police have arrested a 28-year-old woman, accused of killing her 3-year-old daughter by drowning her in Anasagar Lake. The shocking incident came to light after CCTV footage exposed contradictions in her statement.

According to Christian Ganj police, the accused has been identified as Anjali Singh alias Priya (28), wife of Raju, originally from Banaras, Uttar Pradesh. She had separated from her husband and moved to Ajmer, where she worked as a receptionist and entered into a live-in relationship with Alokesh Gupta, a hotel employee.

On Tuesday night, Anjali allegedly took her daughter, Kavya Singh, to Anasagar Chaupati and pushed her into the lake. Initially, she told police and her partner that the child had gone missing near a drain bridge behind City Hospital. She even claimed to have searched the entire night.

However, CCTV footage showed Anjali walking with her daughter near the lake and later returning alone around 1:30 am. This raised suspicion, leading to her interrogation.

By Wednesday morning, Kavya’s body was recovered from the lake. Under questioning, Anjali confessed that she put her daughter to sleep by the lakeside and then pushed her into the water.

DSP Rudra Prakash Sharma confirmed the arrest, stating that Anjali admitted to committing the crime as her live-in partner often taunted her, saying the girl was her first husband’s child. Troubled by the remarks, she decided to eliminate the child.

articles.title: Sikar Honeytrap Gang Busted: Mastermind & Accomplice Arrested for ₹12.9 Lakh Extortion
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Dhod police in Sikar have arrested two women, including the mastermind of a honeytrap gang, for duping and extorting ₹12.90 lakh from a 64-year-old man. Both accused were sent to jail today.

body.html:
The Dhod police in Sikar have arrested two women, including the mastermind of a honeytrap gang, for duping and extorting ₹12.90 lakh from a 64-year-old man. Both accused were sent to jail today.

SHO Rakesh Kumar Meena confirmed the arrest of mastermind Renuka Chaudhary (30), daughter of Bajranglal, resident of Ghassu Ka Bas, and her accomplice Subita (37), wife of Surjaram Jat, resident of Rampura. Police have also frozen Renuka’s bank account.

According to the complaint filed by victim Ramkaran (64) on August 30, he had come in contact with Renuka through Facebook 15–20 days earlier. Renuka made frequent video calls to him and later introduced Subita’s daughter via Instagram. Soon after, the girl visited Ramkaran at his farmhouse, but within minutes, Renuka arrived with accomplices, assaulted him, and snatched a gold ring, a gold chain, and ₹25,000 in cash. Later, Renuka used a stamped signature to transfer ₹12.90 lakh into her account.

Police revealed that Renuka had previously trapped and extorted lakhs from a government doctor in the Laxmangarh police station area. In this case too, she spotted Ramkaran’s resort and conspired with Subita to lure and blackmail him.

Both women, who had been absconding, were tracked down at Dhod Square today and arrested. They have now been remanded to jail.
